note: What a host signs to let its own browser talk to nvoken directly. The host is the identity provider; nvoken verifies the assertion and never learns who the subject is. Minting happens in host backend code and never in a browser. Contract version 2 pins one tenant actor, exact Agent and AgentRevision, one closed memory grant, and one closed Conversation grant. Claims never select operations.

signing_key.note: Base64 of the 32-byte Ed25519 seed and of the 32-byte public key. `public_key` is what `nvoken client-key create --public-key` registers; the seed never leaves the host.

serialization.note: Compact JSON with no insignificant whitespace, top-level members in this order, absent members omitted. Nested grant members use lexical order, so namespace or conversation_id precedes scope. Ed25519 signatures are deterministic, so identical claims produce an identical token in every language — which is what makes `token` below a check rather than an illustration. A verifier parses JSON and does not care about order; this order exists so the SDKs can be held to one byte-exact answer.

refusals.note: A mint helper refuses these rather than producing a token the runtime will reject, so a bad grant fails in the host's own tests instead of in a browser.
cases: blank or whitespace-padded sub, tenant_key, a user memory namespace, or any string claim over 255 characters
a missing or malformed agent_id or agent_revision_id
a missing memory_access or conversation_access grant, an unknown scope, or members that do not match the selected scope
a lifetime of zero or less, or over maximum_lifetime_seconds
any ops claim, including an empty array
iss, kid, agent_id, agent_revision_id, or an exact conversation_id that is not a well-formed id of its kind
